summary: Screw-pile light at the entrance to Tangier Sound, Maryland, lit in 1867; its house was saved in 1966 and now stands at the Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum.

lens.note: Original lens fifth order (chapter and USLHS); USLHS lists the current optic as fourth order; a CBMM photo caption from 1968 describes a third-order lens on loan from the Coast Guard.

structures.note: Present house, cut in two and moved to St. Michaels in 1966

access.note: Exhibit on the grounds of the Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum, St. Michaels

visit.note: Inside the museum exhibit; visitors can climb the sea hatch

events.note: Light station established; lightships marked the Tangier Sound entrance until 1845
First screw-pile house, square, on the north side of the entrance
Carried away by ice on 8 January 1877; keeper and assistant escaped across the ice
Present hexagonal wooden house; the Chesapeake Chapter's page gives 1880 for its erection
New light opened two years after the 1877 loss
Red sector added to the lantern
Steamer Express lost off Hooper's Strait, 23 Oct 1878; papers disagree on the toll and do not mention the light
21 March 1923: keeper McGrath and assistant McDorman rescued the occupant of a small boat near the station
Flashing white minor acetylene light established
Fully automated; the house began to deteriorate
Coast Guard designated the light for destruction; the Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum arranged to save it
House cut in two and barged forty miles to Navy Point, St. Michaels; arrived 9 Nov 1966

wrecks.outcome: Lost off Hooper's Strait; the papers disagree on the toll and do not mention the light
Occupant rescued by keeper McGrath and assistant McDorman near the station

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum (1879) and the Screwpiles book (opened two years after January 1877) point to 1879; the Chesapeake Chapter page gives 1880 with re-erection in October. Not resolved by these sources; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: 1) Dates of the second house: 1879 (CBMM, Screwpiles 'two years later') against 1880 (Chesapeake Chapter 'Hooper Strait Lighthouse' page). Story gives both. 2) Lens order: chapter and USLHS say fifth order originally; USLHS place record lists the current optic as fourth order; a CBMM 1968 photo caption says third order on loan from the USCG. Not reconciled; the lens field is marked unknown. 3) County: USLHS record says Talbot (St. Michaels, where the house now stands); Screwpiles puts the original light in Dorchester County. The map point in the record (38.226748, -76.075596) is the original site in Hooper Strait, not the present house at St. Michaels. Editor to decide how the map shows the move. 4) Express (23 Oct 1878): the Herald headline says twenty of her passengers and crew drowned; the dispatch says all the crew and passengers were lost except for some persons, and the OCR garbles the number. The Gazette has the same loss a day earlier. Neither the Herald nor the Gazette mentions the light; the story says so. The Herald's Hooper's Strait OCR is garbled, so the location quote is from the Gazette. 5) William H. Davis (USLHS obituary in the 1926 Bulletin): he joined in 1881 and is said to have helped build the Hooper Straits light, which fits neither 1879 nor 1880 cleanly; the obituary does not say which work. Not a keeper here, so not in the roster. 6) Bulletin 1923: the rescue is on printed p. 283 (PDF p. 23, read from the page break). OCR garbles the rescue sentence, so the story paraphrases it; the name McDorman is OCR'd as 'McDorlllan' and was matched to Walter F. McDorman on the USLHS roster by name and station, not by OCR column position. 7) LHB 1899: fiscal year taken from the corpus label; the scan page is 142 and the printed page was not read. 8) The 'families not allowed', water from gutters and weekly groceries come from the Chesapeake Chapter page only; no primary source was read for them. 9) The Cornwell/Conway ice story and the 'two weeks stranded' detail come from one book (Screwpiles, p. 94); the book's author and publisher were not visible in the flipbook. Wikipedia's version (with a Cornwell quotation) is unsourced and was not used. 10) Roster: 46 stints from the USLHS roster (NARA-based); no span is 'at least' and none is open-ended. Gatha F. Cottee's sex was not checked; the name alone does not settle it. 11) USCG Historian's Hooper Strait article could not be read (archive copy unreadable, live page blocked), so it is not cited. 12) Page reads over the budget guideline: about 17. Chronicling America and Bulletin pages were read in full where needed for the quotes.
